instructions: The night before, or at least 3 hours ahead, make the marinade. Peel the dry outer layers off the 3 lemongrass stalks, cut off the woody tops and finely mince the pale lower parts. Finely mince the 2 shallots and 4 of the garlic cloves.

In a large bowl, stir the lemongrass, shallots and garlic with 3 tbsp fish sauce, 2 tbsp oyster sauce, 3 tbsp soy sauce, 2 tbsp honey, 2 tbsp brown sugar, 1 tsp black pepper and 3 tbsp of the oil. Add the 2 lbs pork chops and turn them until every side is coated. Cover the bowl and refrigerate it.

At the same time, make the pickles. Peel the 2 carrots and the daikon and cut them into thin matchsticks. In a jar or bowl, stir 1 cup warm water, 1 cup rice vinegar, 1 tsp salt and 2 tbsp sugar until the sugar dissolves. Add the vegetables, push them under the liquid and refrigerate them.
On the day, take the chops out of the fridge 20 minutes before they go in the oven. Heat the oven to 400°F and set a wire rack on a foil-lined baking sheet.

Rinse 2 cups broken rice in a sieve until the water runs mostly clear. Put it in a medium pot with 2 1/2 cups water and bring it to a boil over high heat. Cover it, turn the heat to low and cook for 15 minutes. Take it off the heat and leave it covered for 10 minutes.
Meanwhile, lift the chops out of the marinade, let the extra drip back into the bowl and lay them on the rack in a single layer. Keep the marinade in the bowl. Bake them for 10 minutes.

Flip the chops and brush the tops with the marinade left in the bowl. Bake them for 8 to 10 minutes. You're cooking them to 145°F in the thickest part, so if you have a thermometer, check them there. No thermometer? Cut next to the bone. They're done when the juices run clear and the meat is only faintly pink.
Turn the oven to broil and broil the chops for 2 to 3 minutes, until the edges char in spots. Stay close. The honey burns quickly. Transfer them to a plate and let them rest for 5 minutes.

While the chops bake, make the scallion oil. Thinly slice 4 green onions and put them in a small heatproof bowl with 1/4 tsp salt. Heat 3 tbsp of the oil in a small pan over medium-high heat for about 1 minute, until it shimmers. Pour it over the green onions. They'll sizzle and turn bright green.

Make the nuoc cham. Juice the 2 limes. That should be about 1/4 cup. In a bowl, stir 3 tbsp fish sauce, 3 tbsp sugar and 3/4 cup warm water until the sugar dissolves. Stir in the lime juice and the last garlic clove, minced. Taste it, and add a spoonful of water if it's too salty.
Thinly slice the chilli and put it in a small bowl. Slice the cucumber and the 2 tomatoes. Drain the pickles.

Heat the last 1 tbsp of oil in a large nonstick skillet over medium heat. Crack in the 4 eggs and cook them for about 3 minutes, until the whites are set and the edges are crisp, with the yolks still runny.

Spoon the rice onto 4 plates and spoon the scallion oil over it. Add a pork chop, a fried egg, the cucumber, tomato and pickles to each plate. Serve with the nuoc cham and the sliced chilli on the side.
advance_prep_notes: Marinate the pork chops and make the pickles the night before, or at least 3 hours ahead.
method_notes: All three versions marinate the chops in lemongrass, shallot, garlic and a sweet, salty mix of fish sauce, oyster sauce and soy, and serve them on rice. Cooking Therapy, the lead, marinates for 3 hours or overnight, bakes the chops on a rack and brushes them with the marinade at the flip, and builds the full broken rice plate with a fried egg, pickled carrot and daikon, cucumber, tomato, scallion oil and nuoc cham. Wok and Kin adds five spice and finishes with a honey glaze under the grill, and Delightful Plate grills thin chops over high heat in a few minutes. This one uses a hotter oven than the lead plus a short broil to char the edges, adds a little sugar to the lead's pickle brine, and keeps the chilli on the side.
